newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo chief says bank will cut rates.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo chief says bank will cut rates.

text.p: The chairman of Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino, Gianni Zandano, said on Thursday that his bank would follow the Bank of Italy's move in cutting interest rates.

"I think we will fall in line as well but frankly we have not thought about it yet," Zandano told reporters in Milan. "I would be very surprised if there were some resistance to the adjustment on the part of the banking system."
The central bank cut its discount rate to 7.50 percent on Wednesday night from 8.25 percent.
San Paolo's prime rate currently stands at 10.25 percent, 0.5 percentage point lower than most other banks before the latest Bank of Italy discount rate cut.

Earlier Monte dei Paschi di Siena became the first big commercial bank to announce a new cut in its prime rate, which it brought down to 10 percent from 10.75 percent while its top rate was reduced to 17.75 percent from 18.50 percent. Milan newsroom +39266102321
